name: China economy
summary: China's official manufacturing and composite PMIs fell below 50 in October; no contagion
state: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October and the composite output index to 49.7, down 1.0 point, with construction at 48.0 (National Bureau of Statistics, 1 Nov). Growth was 4.5% in Q3, near target, and no property-developer default wave or financial contagion had been reported as of 6 Nov, so Normal holds under hysteresis, but momentum is weakening.
for_you: A slowdown in China tends to weigh on commodity exporters and on firms that depend on Chinese consumer and construction demand.
rubric_hit: Growth near official target and no contagion (Normal); official PMIs below 50 in October

sources.title: National Bureau of Statistics of China — Purchasing Managers' Index for October 2026

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
